official.deadline_note: The FES publishes degree-stage windows rather than a single closing date. Master: before or at the beginning of the first university semester of the master's programme - winter semester by 30 November, summer semester by 31 May. Bachelor / Diplom / Magister / Staatsexamen: after the first semester and up to three semesters before the end of the standard period of study. Medicine: after the fourth semester or the Physikum, until the end of the sixth semester.
official.application_cycle: No annual cycle is published; applications are accepted continuously provided the degree-stage windows are met
official.status_note: The programme page states that applications are formally possible both from within Germany and from abroad ('Bewerbungen sind formell sowohl aus Deutschland als auch aus dem Ausland möglich') and links applicants directly to the online application form; no closure of the programme is announced.
official.tuition_coverage_note: No statement about tuition, fees or fee waivers is published anywhere on the FES pages for this programme. The published benefit is the monthly financial support, the health-insurance costs taken over and the child supplement.
benefits: Financial support of 992 Euro per month, plus health-insurance costs taken over and an additional 255 Euro per month for scholarship holders with children
Extensive programme of socio-political seminars, workshops and competence training

Stipendiary groups in numerous cities plus 18 thematic working groups across regions, and integration into the network of current and former scholarship holders, many of whom act as mentors on study and career questions
The scholarship does not have to be repaid and is awarded independently of any legal entitlement
Travel costs incurred for an invitation to a selection interview can be reimbursed on request using the published form
eligibility: You are a foreign national - the FAQ restricts this to nationals outside the EU, from the former CIS states, Asia (except Japan), Africa and South America; students from OECD states such as the USA, Australia, New Zealand and Japan cannot be funded
You are already studying at a German state or state-recognised university or university of applied sciences, and first graded performance records are a prerequisite for applying

Foreign applicants must not have been in the Federal Republic of Germany for longer than 15 months at the time of application (exempt: those who came to study, to do a doctorate or other academic work or to prepare for it, e.g. a language course or Studienkolleg, and people after a successful refugee-status recognition)
You have very good German language skills - a level of B2 is accepted even without a certificate, and proof is required even if the degree programme is taught in English
You have above-average grades in your studies, measured against the average of the subject at the university location
You are socially and politically engaged and identify with the values of social democracy (freedom, justice and solidarity)
requirements: Applications have to be submitted in German, because German language skills are a requirement for the scholarship
Application via the online application form for the Grundförderung für Ausländer:innen; documents are only requested after the online form has been reviewed
Bachelor's students must submit their first graded performance records
You must already be in Germany and be studying at a German university
You must be available for selection interviews in Germany; longer stays abroad during the procedure can lead to the procedure being discontinued
After the request you have three weeks for the documents and up to six weeks for the expert opinions
documents: Motivationsschreiben (letter of motivation), potentially more detailed than in the online form
Gap-free tabular CV plus an out-spelled detailed CV in continuous prose of at most two pages
Abiturzeugnis or another higher-education entrance qualification - certified copies are not required
Immatrikulationsbescheinigung showing the subject and the number of semesters (a Studienplatzzusage suffices initially for master's programmes), plus the Studienverlaufsplan on the FES template

University certificate of all study and examination achievements obtained so far, with a self-compiled chronological overview by semester if these are not shown; Bachelor certificate for master's applicants, or a provisional one if not yet issued
Only for foreign and refugee applicants: a language certificate (Sprachzeugnis) and a copy of the residence status
Short presentation of your current economic situation; where applicable a passport photo and chronological certificates of vocational training and employment

Two expert opinions (Gutachten) from university teachers - these must be sent by the referees themselves, as PDF without password protection, on university letterhead or stamp, maximum 1 MB, to the responsible FES contact person
selection_criteria: Above-average talent and performance, assessed against the standards of the chosen subject at the university location, including a positive prognosis for completing the standard period of study
Personality: suitability as a member of the scholarship-holder group at the university location, team ability and social competence
Social and political engagement: interest in socio-political questions, level of information, existing engagement that fits the foundation's environment, or recognisable potential
Identification with the fundamental values of social democracy and socio-political commitment

Particular consideration is given to applicants who are the first in their family to study and/or have a migration background, to women, and to students at universities of applied sciences and in STEM subjects
Overall verdict by each referee of particularly funding-worthy, funding-worthy or not funding-worthy
coverage: Financial support of 992 Euro per month
Costs for health insurance are taken over
Additional 255 Euro per month for scholarship holders with children
Travel costs for selection interviews are reimbursable on request
The scholarship is not repayable and is awarded independently of any legal entitlement
application_method: Complete and submit the online application form for the Grundförderung für Ausländer:innen with personal details, professional and family background, motivation and socio-political engagement
Within two to four weeks receive either a rejection or the request to submit documents and expert opinions
Upload the documents through the online portal within three weeks; the two Gutachten must be sent by the referees within up to six weeks
Attend the first selection interview, a subject-related conversation with a trust lecturer (Vertrauensdozentin/Vertrauensdozent) from which an expert opinion is produced
Attend the second selection interview with a member of the selection committee, which produces a further expert opinion
Decision by the selection committee, which meets eight to ten times a year; the applicant is informed at the latest one week after the relevant meeting
official.application_route: Online FES application form for the Grundförderung für Ausländer:innen in German, followed by a document upload in the FES portal and two selection interviews.
official.study_mode: Full-time degree programme; part-time and extra-occupational study is not funded, and dual programmes are eligible only if full-time study is evidenced
official.citizenship_residency: Only nationals outside the EU, from the former CIS states, Asia (except Japan), Africa and South America; not students from OECD states such as the USA, Australia, New Zealand or Japan. Austrians and other EU citizens apply to the FES programmes aimed at Germans and Bildungsinländer:innen. You must already be in Germany and normally have been there no longer than 15 months.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the programme exists specifically for foreign nationals already studying in Germany; the English information page states that it is essential to live in Germany and study at a German university.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: All fields of study are funded, including artistic degree programmes. Not funded: medical studies up to and including the preliminary medical examination, doctoral degrees and further training in medicine, physiotherapy training, further training as psychological psychotherapist, Studienkolleg, language courses, second degrees (unless the first degree was not publicly funded), short courses of study under three semesters, research visits, trainee programmes, project proposals, short stays abroad, study-abroad programmes outside the EU, pure final-examination phases and postdoc projects.
official.description: The Friedrich-Ebert-Stiftung's basic funding programme for foreign nationals supports international students at German public or state-recognised universities with a monthly stipend, health-insurance cover and a wide socio-political seminar and mentoring programme, so that holders can concentrate on their studies and their engagement without financial worries. The scholarship is not repayable and requires very good German, above-average grades and identification with the values of social democracy.

not_confirmed: duration - no maximum funding period or standard duration is published for the Grundförderung
tuition_coverage - the FES pages publish no tuition or fee component, only the monthly stipend, health insurance and the child supplement
travel_coverage - no travel allowance for holders; only travel to a selection interview is reimbursable on request
english_requirement - no English language requirement is published; German is the mandatory language throughout
child supplement amount - the German programme page states 255 EUR per month while the English summary page lists a 276 EUR family allowance
verification.notes: The 992 EUR monthly amount, health-insurance cover, 255 EUR child supplement, B2 language rule and the 30 November / 31 May degree-stage windows were read directly on the Grundförderung für Ausländer:innen page. The country restriction, the 15-month rule, the requirement to already be in Germany and the second-degree rule came from the FES FAQ on the funding of foreign students. The document list, format and size limits (PDF/JPG, 1 MB per document, 4 MB total, three weeks) and the referee submission route came from the official 'Benötigte Unterlagen und Hinweise zur Erstellung von Gutachten' checklist dated November 2025 on fes.de.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a living stipend of 992 EUR a month plus health-insurance cover and 255 EUR if you have children, not a tuition scholarship - flights, semester contributions and any fees stay on you. Two gates decide almost everything: your passport and your German. Only nationals from outside the EU (Asia except Japan, Africa, Latin America, the former CIS states, eastern and south-eastern Europe) qualify, and B2 German must be provable even when your degree is taught entirely in English. Add the 15-month rule on how long you have already been in Germany and the fact that the committee sits only eight to ten times a year, and the realistic timeline from form to decision is three to seven months.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-EU students already enrolled at a German public or state-recognised university with B2 German, above-average grades and a documented record of social or political engagement.
application_readiness_checklist: Check your nationality against the country rule before anything else - US, Australian, New Zealand and Japanese nationals are excluded, and EU citizens belong in the sibling programme
Count your months in Germany against the 15-month rule and collect the evidence that you came here to study (language course, Studienkolleg, enrolment) if you are over it
Line up two university referees early and give them the deadline in writing, because they must send the Gutachten themselves and they get up to six weeks
Compress scans into PDF or JPG only, keeping every single file under 1 MB and the complete set under 4 MB
Block out three calendar weeks after the invitation to submit documents, and diarise 30 November (winter) / 31 May (summer)
Keep any side income in mind: the English information page states that income exceeding 400 EUR per month is credited against the scholarship
common_rejection_risks: Holding a nationality that is excluded by the OECD rule, or applying as an EU citizen to the wrong FES programme
Missing the degree-stage window - a master's application must land before or at the start of the first master's semester
Being over the 15-month stay in Germany without the exemption that applies to those who came to study
Motivation text that lists grades but shows no socio-political engagement or identification with social democracy
Referees sending their Gutachten late, or sending them to you instead of directly to the FES contact person
Long stays abroad during the procedure, which can cause the process to be discontinued
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Semester and social-fee contributions, any tuition your institution charges, flights and visa fees, rent above what the stipend covers, study materials, and any side income above 400 EUR a month that is credited against the scholarship.
document_audit: Only PDF and JPG are accepted, with a hard 1 MB limit per document and 4 MB for the whole set - scan at a resolution you can afford
The two Gutachten cannot be uploaded by you; if a referee emails them to you rather than to FES they will not be considered

For master's applicants a provisional Bachelor certificate is enough if the final one is not yet issued, but the Immatrikulationsbescheinigung must show subject and semester count (a Studienplatzzusage works first)
Foreign and refugee applicants must additionally add the language certificate and a copy of the residence status
Certificates do not need to be certified copies, but they must be legible and complete - gaps cost you the three-week window
New performance records obtained during the procedure must be emailed to FES without delay, again under 1 MB
alerts: From application to decision takes three to seven months, gated by committee meetings eight to ten times a year, so never budget the money for the very next semester
A home-country Bachelor followed by a German Bachelor or Master is possible; it only counts as a second degree if the first degree was publicly funded
Asylum seekers can apply for the regular foreign-student programme and may additionally be assessed for the FES Solidaritätsfonds
The German programme page states 255 EUR and the English summary page 276 EUR for the child/family allowance - confirm the current figure with your FES contact person before you budget on it
No reasons are given for a rejection, and rejected applications with all documents are kept for up to three years before deletion
Interviews happen in Germany, so keep short absences around the invitation window
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit the online form in German, get a yes/no within two to four weeks, upload the documents within three weeks and get the Gutachten in within six, then a trust-lecturer interview, a committee interview, and a decision notified within a week of the relevant committee session.

official.deadline_note: Two fixed rounds per year: applications close on 15 January and 15 July. The 15 July 2026 round has already passed, so the next closure is 15 January 2027. The general KAS FAQ confirms the 15 January / 15 July dates for the Studien- and Promotionsförderung.
official.application_cycle: Two application rounds a year, 15 January and 15 July
official.status_note: The programme page states 'Please apply online on campus.kas.de until 15 January or 15 July annually'; with 15 July 2026 past, the next round is the one closing on 15 January 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: No tuition or fee coverage is published on any of the KAS pages for this programme; the pages list only the monthly financial support, the study- or research-expense allowances and the seminar and network programme.
benefits: Undergraduate and graduate students: financial support depending on your income or the income of your parents, up to 752 Euros per month, plus 300 Euro for study-related expenses such as books and writing material
PhD candidates: financial support of 1350 Euros per month plus 100 Euro for research-related expenses, with further allowances possible
Wide range of seminars on salient political, economic, academic and cultural topics, plus integration into the local Hochschulgruppe with Vertrauensdozierende who advise on study questions
Access to an extended network of fellow scholarship holders and alumni (over 17,000 alumni), with intensive exchange and exclusive access to professional contacts for PhD candidates
Career counselling and support with your first steps into the labour market

PhD candidates: individual support in all matters regarding the PhD and scholarship from Graduate Student Support Department staff and special academic advisors at your university, plus encounters with personalities from the public sector
eligibility: As a refugee in Germany you are entitled under the specific legal requirements to study and to apply for a scholarship - for instance with the Konrad-Adenauer-Stiftung

Residence permit according to paragraph 16 or 18 AufenthG: apply for the KAS international programme (Master's and PhD); residence permit according to paragraph 24 AufenthG or paragraph 61 BAFoG: apply for Studienfoerderung (Bachelor's and Master's) and Promotionsfoerderung (PhD)
You have completed your schooling and studies with above-average grades
You identify with the political stances represented by the Konrad Adenauer Foundation
You are involved in voluntary work in political, social and cultural areas and are willing to actively participate in the scholarship programme
You are interested in a broad range of topics beyond your research area and appreciate exchange in a multicultural environment
requirements: Apply online on campus.kas.de until 15 January or 15 July annually
Upload all required application documents as part of the online application; documents are submitted digitally only, and KAS contacts applicants directly if paper is ever needed
Proof of German language skills at B2 level (undergraduate and graduate students)
PhD candidates: proof of advanced German language skills at least equivalent to the Goethe-Zertifikat C1 - a language certificate is required for the application
PhD candidates: your supervisor is familiar with your proposal and supports your application
documents: Written-out and tabular curriculum vitae of up to three pages (undergraduate and graduate students)
Certified copy of the admission letter from your German university
Letter of assessment of your academic skills, e.g. by a professor at your university
Copy of the transcript of your university grades and courses or single course certificates, and the matriculation certificate
Copy of all your academic diploma and training certificates
Proof of German language skills at B2 level (undergraduate and graduate students) or at least equivalent to the Goethe-Zertifikat C1 with a certificate (PhD candidates)

PhD candidates additionally: application form on your professional and personal development and social or political engagement; written-out, signed and dated CV of 4,000-6,000 characters including spaces plus a signed and dated tabular CV; certified copy of your examination certificate or university diploma; two letters of assessment by your supervisor and another professor entitled to supervise a doctoral thesis, not older than six months before the deadline and submitted by you; and a PhD project proposal of five to ten pages with 1.5 line spacing, 12 pt font and a literature appendix
selection_criteria: Open-mindedness, high commitment and a wide range of interests
Above-average learning or academic achievements at school or university
Social engagement and willingness to assume social and political responsibility
Identification with the values and views of the Konrad-Adenauer-Stiftung

PhD proposals are judged on high actuality and social and/or political relevance of the topic, an overview of the main problems and solution approaches, research design and methods, and a tentative timeframe
coverage: Undergraduate and graduate students: income-dependent financial support of up to 752 Euros per month plus 300 Euro for study-related expenses (books, writing material etc.)
PhD candidates: 1,350 Euros per month plus 100 Euro for research-related expenses, with further allowances possible
Seminars on political, economic, academic and cultural topics, the local Hochschulgruppe with Vertrauensdozierende, and access to the network of over 17,000 alumni
Career counselling and support with the first steps into the labour market; individual support for PhD candidates from KAS staff and academic advisors at the university
application_method: Confirm which residence-permit route applies to you (paragraph 16 or 18 AufenthG for the international programme, paragraph 24 AufenthG or paragraph 61 BAFoG for Studien- and Promotionsfoerderung)
Assemble the document set for your degree stage, including the certified admission letter and the German language certificate
Apply online on campus.kas.de before the round closes on 15 January or 15 July and upload all documents
official.application_route: Apply online through campus.kas.de and upload the complete document set before the round closes on 15 January or 15 July.
official.citizenship_residency: Refugees in Germany with a residence permit under paragraph 16 or 18 AufenthG (routed to the international programme, Master's and PhD) or under paragraph 24 AufenthG or paragraph 61 BAFoG (routed to Studienfoerderung for Bachelor's and Master's and to Promotionsfoerderung for PhD).
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the programme is for refugees in Germany, and the KAS publishes the same information bilingually in English and Ukrainian on this page.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: All fields are supported in the Studienfoerderung; the KAS Promotionsfoerderung funds doctoral theses of all disciplines except human and dental medicine.
official.research_requirement: PhD candidates must submit a proposal of five to ten pages (1.5 line spacing, 12 pt font, literature appendix) that shows high actuality and social and/or political relevance, the main problems and solution approaches, the research design and methods, and a tentative timeframe; the doctoral supervisor must be familiar with the proposal and support the application. The proposal is also judged on content and language.
official.description: The Konrad-Adenauer-Stiftung supports refugees in Germany who are entitled to study under the specific legal requirements, offering monthly financial support, a study-expense allowance and a broad seminar, mentoring and alumni programme at Bachelor's, Master's and PhD level. The foundation looks for above-average academic achievement, voluntary engagement and identification with its political values, and applications are made online through campus.kas.de twice a year.

not_confirmed: duration - no maximum funding period or standard duration is published for this programme
tuition_coverage - KAS publishes no tuition or fee coverage, only the monthly support and the expense allowances
travel_coverage - no travel allowance or travel-cost reimbursement is published for holders
exact monthly amount for an individual applicant - the page publishes 'up to 752 Euros' depending on income, not a fixed figure
english_requirement - no English language requirement is published; German is the required language throughout
verification.notes: kas.de blocks generic HTTP fetchers at its web application firewall (HTTP 403 with an event ID), so the pages were read in a real browser session and the content was taken verbatim from the German/English version of the refugee page itself. The 752 EUR / 1,350 EUR figures, the 300 EUR and 100 EUR allowances, the 15 January and 15 July rounds, the complete document lists and the paragraph 16/18/24/61 BAFoG routing were confirmed on that page; the no-reapplication rule, the digital-only submission, the translation and grade-conversion rule and the reference-language rule came from the KAS general application FAQ.

applicant_utility.summary: Two gates decide this scholarship long before grades matter: your residence permit and your German. Holders of paragraph 24 AufenthG or paragraph 61 BAFoG belong in the Studien- and Promotionsfoerderung for Bachelor's, Master's and PhD, while paragraph 16 and 18 holders are routed to the separate international programme instead. The published ceiling is up to 752 EUR a month plus 300 EUR for books and materials for undergraduate and graduate students, and 1,350 EUR plus 100 EUR research expenses at PhD level, but the undergraduate figure is means-tested so the real amount can be lower. There are only two attempts a year, on 15 January and 15 July, and KAS rules out any reapplication after a rejection.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Refugees in Germany with a qualifying residence permit, above-average results, a documented voluntary-engagement record and B2 (PhD: C1) German.
application_readiness_checklist: Establish your permit type first - paragraph 24 or 61 BAFoG for the domestic routes, paragraph 16 or 18 for the international programme - because the wrong route wastes a round
Get the admission letter certified; KAS asks for a certified copy, not a plain scan

Ask your professor for the assessment letter early, and for a PhD application secure two: your supervisor plus another professor entitled to supervise a doctorate, both under six months old at the deadline
Have foreign school-leaving and degree certificates translated and certified, with the average or final grade converted to the German scale
Write the flowing CV to the page limit (up to three pages; PhD: 4,000-6,000 characters including spaces) and make sure both CVs carry your name and date of birth
Build the PhD proposal to the explicit criteria - actuality, social and political relevance, problems, methods, timeframe - and have your supervisor confirm support in writing
common_rejection_risks: Applying through the wrong programme because of a paragraph 16 or 18 permit, which the page routes to the international programme instead
German below B2 for undergraduate and graduate applicants, or below C1 without a certificate for PhD candidates
Assessment letters older than six months before the deadline, or written by someone not entitled to supervise a doctoral thesis
An engagement story that is asserted rather than evidenced, since voluntary work and identification with KAS values are scored as heavily as grades
A PhD proposal that reads like a project plan instead of research, missing the state of research or the methodological design
Reapplying in a later round after an earlier KAS rejection, which the foundation does not allow
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Semester contributions and any tuition at your institution, residence-permit and visa fees, travel, and everything above the income-tested monthly amount plus the 300 EUR study allowance - KAS publishes no tuition or travel coverage.
document_audit: Foreign school-leaving and academic certificates need a certified translation and a conversion of the average or final grade
The admission letter must be a certified copy, and the matriculation certificate is requested in addition to it
Both CV formats are required - a flowing, out-spelled one and a tabular one - each carrying name and date of birth
For a PhD application you submit the two assessment letters yourself through the portal, and they must be no older than six months before the deadline
References are accepted in German, English and French only (German or English for the Promotionsfoerderung); anything else needs a certified translation
Everything is digital; KAS only asks for paper in individual cases after contacting you
alerts: A rejection is final - KAS states that after a rejection an application at a later date is not possible, so do not treat 15 January and 15 July as two cheap attempts
The undergraduate and graduate amount is means-tested against your own and your parents' income, so 752 EUR is a ceiling rather than a promise
Health insurance, semester contributions and family costs are not part of the published benefit
Allow time before the deadline for the certified translation and grade conversion of foreign certificates
The programme page is published in English and Ukrainian, but the assessment language in practice is German, so prepare the submission in German
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Confirm your residence-permit route, assemble the degree-stage document set, then upload everything through campus.kas.de before the 15 January or 15 July closure and await the assessment.
